\chapter{Bitwise Operations on Arrays}
\label{ch:bitwise}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{Split every number into bits and solve 30 easy problems instead of one hard one; and use the fact that OR and AND change only $\bigO{\log V}$ times.}}
\end{tcolorbox}

\chapterfacts{1400}{2300}{5}{10}{30}

\begin{plannedbox}[Planned Contents --- this chapter is not written yet]
\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item XOR identities: cancelling pairs, prefix XOR, XOR of a range of integers
    \item Per-bit decomposition: counting, sums and choices bit by bit from the top
    \item OR and AND over subarrays: at most $\log V$ distinct values ending at each index
    \item Maximum XOR by greedy over bits (binary tries are the string and tree books)
    \item Bit tricks on arrays: masks of present values, subsets of small arrays
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Part B --- Patterns} (with candidate problems, checked when the chapter is written)

    \item \textbf{Per-bit decomposition}
    \item \textbf{Distinct OR and AND values of subarrays} --- Bitwise ORs of Subarrays {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 898)}
    \item \textbf{Greedy over bits}
    \item \textbf{Prefix XOR}
\end{enumerate}
